gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 29?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 29 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

**Official National Weather Service forecasts for August 31, 2026, in New York City consistently indicate a daytime high in the lower 80s°F (around 81–83°F), with partly sunny skies after morning clouds, light north-to-southeast winds, and only a 20% chance of showers.** This aligns closely with the market's leading bins (80–81°F at 29.5%, 78–79°F at 26.0%, and 82–83°F at 21.5%), reflecting trader consensus around these guidance values.

Key differentiating factors include the extent of morning cloud cover versus afternoon solar heating, subtle differences in low-level wind direction that modulate coastal marine influence or warm advection, and the precise timing or intensity of any scattered showers, which could briefly limit peak temperatures. Ensemble model spreads at this short lead time (roughly two days out) remain modest but allow for small adjustments in the exact maximum, particularly if a stronger ridge or drier air mass materializes. Late-August climatology for the region supports highs near 82°F as a baseline, so current guidance sits right at seasonal norms with limited deviation expected absent a major pattern shift. Updated model runs and NWS briefings in the next 24–48 hours will likely refine these probabilities further.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast consensus from multiple numerical weather prediction models places Munich’s maximum temperature on August 31 near 24–25 °C, driving the market’s heavy weighting toward those outcomes. Persistent westerly flow, increasing cloud cover, and a 40–80 % chance of showers or thunderstorms during the day are expected to limit solar heating and cap the afternoon peak, consistent with late-August climatology where the long-term average high is 22.4 °C. Recent model runs have shown little shift in this range, leaving only modest implied probability for 26 °C or higher under clearer, drier scenarios. Traders are therefore pricing in the narrow uncertainty band typical of a 24-hour forecast horizon.

Persistent westerly flow, increasing cloud cover, and a 40–80 % chance of showers or thunderstorms during the day are expected to limit solar heating and cap the afternoon peak, consistent with late-August climatology where the long-term average high is 22.4 °C. Recent model runs have shown little shift in this range, leaving only modest implied probability for 26 °C or higher under clearer, drier scenarios. Traders are therefore pricing in the narrow uncertainty band typical of a 24-hour forecast horizon.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 31 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and global models indicate a mostly cloudy Monday for Tokyo with easterly flow and a modest chance of afternoon showers or thunderstorms, limiting peak insolation and capping the daily maximum near 29–31 °C. Persistent marine air and high humidity further moderate temperatures by enhancing cloud cover and reducing daytime heating rates. Model consensus shows only modest spread around these values, with differences between 29 °C and 31 °C hinging on the exact timing of any breaks in the overcast and the strength of the sea-breeze circulation. Historical August normals near 30 °C provide context, yet the current pattern of post-frontal stabilization favors outcomes clustered in the upper 20s to low 30s rather than extremes. Updated model runs and JMA briefings tomorrow morning will refine the final observed maximum before market resolution.

A 30–40% chance of afternoon showers or thunderstorms introduces the main variable: early or widespread cloud build-up could cap the high near 80–81°F, while delayed or localized convection would permit readings in the 82–83°F range before any cooling.

Historical verification for similar late-August patterns shows highs often verifying 1–2°F below point forecasts when marine influence strengthens, contributing to the slight market tilt toward the lower bin. With resolution imminent, traders monitor real-time observations and the final model runs for boundary-layer mixing and dewpoint trends that will determine whether the peak lands in the leading ranges.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 30 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Cloud cover, light northerly winds, and elevated humidity are the dominant factors capping Tokyo's peak temperature on August 30, 2026. Official Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and multiple numerical models indicate widespread stratiform clouds persisting through midday, limiting surface insolation and yielding a forecast high of 26–28 °C. Recent observations show a modest cooling trend after earlier August heat, with dew points near 20–22 °C supporting only modest sensible heating even under brief afternoon breaks in cloud. The tight 26 °C (49 %) versus 27 °C (42 %) split in market-implied odds reflects residual model spread in boundary-layer mixing and the exact timing of any partial clearing; a modest increase in solar exposure or slightly stronger southerly flow could push the maximum to 27–28 °C, while continued overcast keeps it at or below 26 °C.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from numerical weather prediction models positions 24–25°C as the most probable maximum temperature range for Munich on August 31.** Multiple sources, including GFS-based guidance and European models, indicate a daytime high near or slightly above the long-term average of 22.4°C for the date, driven by moderate westerly flow, partial clearing after early showers, and limited daytime heating under increasing cloud cover or scattered precipitation.

Key atmospheric factors include a transitioning synoptic pattern with west-to-southwest winds of 10–20 km/h, surface temperatures rising from morning lows around 15–17°C to afternoon peaks before any additional cooling from showers. Model runs show light rain or showers mainly in the morning (precipitation probabilities 20–60% early, dropping sharply later), followed by mostly clear to partly cloudy skies that cap insolation and prevent stronger warming.

This setup aligns with typical late-August conditions in the region, where historical records show highs ranging from the low teens to over 32°C but cluster around the low-to-mid 20s in non-extreme years. Recent model updates have held steady on these values with only minor spread, supporting the market's heavy weighting toward 25°C (55.5%) and 24°C (24.0%), while lower probabilities for 26°C+ reflect limited upside potential from any unexpected clearing or southerly advection. Final official readings from stations such as München-Nymphenburg will resolve the market.

Traders appear to weigh these factors against the potential for partial afternoon clearing that could allow readings to reach 31 °C, producing the close spread between the two leading outcomes. **Current forecasts for Munich on September 1, 2026, show a daily maximum around 22–23°C under stable, partly cloudy conditions with light westerly winds and low precipitation risk.** Multiple models, including GFS-based and ensemble outputs from sources like WeatherBug, The Weather Outlook, and others updated August 30, consistently project highs near 72–73°F (22–23°C), close to or slightly below early-September climatological norms of roughly 21–22°C for the city.

This positions 23°C and 24°C as the leading market outcomes because numerical weather prediction runs emphasize modest daytime heating without strong advection of warmer air masses or clear-sky amplification. Minor model spreads and timing of any residual cloud cover explain the 45% and 24.5% implied probabilities for 24°C and 23°C, respectively, while lower odds for 22°C or 25°C+ reflect the narrow expected range and limited upside potential from current atmospheric patterns. With resolution imminent, any final model updates or observational tweaks in the next 48 hours could still influence exact peak readings within this tight band.

**Forecast models from the National Weather Service and supporting guidance place the expected daily maximum in New York City on August 30, 2026, in the low-to-mid 80s, with official point forecasts calling for highs near 83–84 °F under partly sunny skies.** 

Afternoon southwest winds of 5–10 mph and a 30–50 % chance of showers or thunderstorms after midday introduce the main source of uncertainty, as convective activity or increased cloud cover can cap peak temperatures below model guidance. This aligns directly with trader positioning: the 82–83 °F bin leads at 55 % implied probability, followed by 80–81 °F at 26 %, reflecting a tight consensus around seasonal norms (historical average high near 81 °F) while discounting higher bins (84–85 °F at only 13.5 %) due to the storm risk and modest recent cooling trends in late August. 

Early-morning observations in the mid-60s and stable model runs overnight have reinforced rather than shifted these odds, leaving limited room for outcomes outside the 80–85 °F window absent an unexpected clearance or intensification of convection.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Resolution hinges on official Japan Meteorological Agency maximum readings tomorrow.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 31 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 1 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 31 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from official sources points to a daytime high of 22°C in London on August 31, 2026, aligning with the market's leading outcome at 55.5% implied probability.** Multiple model runs, including GFS data referenced in recent briefings, show partly cloudy skies with westerly winds moderating temperatures, producing afternoon peaks near 22°C (around 71–72°F) before cooling overnight.

This matches the long-term August 31 average high of approximately 21.9°C at London Heathrow while reflecting current steering patterns that prevent significant warming or cooling. Nearby 21°C (21% probability) and 23°C (18.5%) remain plausible given minor model spread and typical observation uncertainty of 1°C, whereas outcomes above 24°C carry low odds consistent with the absence of warm advection or clear-sky amplification. Updated Met Office guidance through late August 30 has held steady, supporting trader focus on the narrow 21–23°C band ahead of final verification.

Historical verification for similar late-August setups shows urban stations often run a degree or two cooler than raw model guidance once boundary-layer mixing and marine influence are accounted for. With resolution tied to the daily maximum at LaGuardia and minimal spread in guidance, traders have priced the outcome as a narrow contest driven by whether afternoon destabilization arrives early enough to cap the peak below 82°F.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 30 Aug '26.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Recent cooler conditions and persistent cloud cover are the main drivers keeping trader consensus clustered around 29–30°C for Tokyo’s August 31 high.** Official Japan Meteorological Agency guidance issued August 30 calls for mostly cloudy skies with a forecast high of 31°C and only modest precipitation chances, yet actual highs on August 29–30 reached just 27.5°C amid rain and overcast skies. Key differentiating variables include the degree of afternoon solar heating under variable cloud decks, the strength and persistence of northeasterly flow that can enhance marine cooling, and urban heat-island modulation at the official observation site. With model runs showing only small differences in maximum temperature under these conditions, markets assign the highest implied probabilities to 29°C (39.5%) and 30°C (31.5%), reflecting the narrow uncertainty band around the official outlook.
